text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Police cracked down on a wave of robberies of children by children in Oslo, rounding up 11 immigrant youths aged 12 to 18 suspected of involvement in up to 31 such robberies in the past few months. Police suspect Norwegian children were also members of the robber gangs.

- A review of takeovers in Scandinavian shipping companies in the last two years presented by Wilh. Wilhelmsen ASA shows that the big shipping companies in Norway are getting bigger. The largest companies have increased their share of the market by takeovers, mergers, building of new ships or buying ships.

- Norway's defence forces have personnel problems. In the next few months half of the fighter plane pilots will leave to begin careers as civilian pilots. One third of the submarines are stuck in port because of a lack of crews.

- Per Saevik, head of the Norwegian shipowners association, has bought 12 supply ships from Viking Supply ships for one billion crowns. Saevik and his partners will form a new company which may be listed on the Oslo Bourse.

- Trond Giske, head of the ruling Labour Party's youth league, says Energy and Industry Minister Jens Stoltenberg controls Environment Minister Torbjoern Berntsen. Giske says the Labour government's environmental policy poses a violation of the party programme.
